description:
Hello from Uruguay! 🇺🇾🚀

We are DFANV, a team of students from Santa Elena School in Uruguay, excited to participate in the NASA Space Apps Challenge! 🌎✨
summary: The Fire in Microgravity is an interactive display that explains how fire behaves in space and why it is one of the biggest dangers for astronauts. Our team built a painted cardboard panel with a tablet embedded in it. The tablet runs an interactive application, created with the help of AI, that works like a control panel about fire safety in space exploration and includes information from NASA experiments such as Saffire and FLEX. Next to the screen, we drew a comparison table showing the differences between fire on Earth and in space: on Earth, flames are long and point upward because hot gases rise, while in microgravity flames become round or spherical, can spread in all directions, and can burn at lower temperatures. Understanding these differences is essential to keep astronauts safe on the space station and on future missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
What it does and how it works. Our project has two parts that work together:

  1. The physical panel: a cardboard board that we painted blue and decorated with rockets. It includes a drawing of two candles, one burning on Earth and one in space, and a handmade table comparing fire in both places by flame shape, gravity, oxygen, movement, temperature and danger.
  2. The interactive application: a tablet built into the panel runs an app that simulates an interactive control panel about fire safety in space, with information about real NASA experiments.

What visitors learn. Without gravity, hot air does not rise, so flames do not point upward. Oxygen reaches the flame more slowly, so flames become round and can burn at lower temperatures. Fire can spread in any direction, and smoke and gases can be very dangerous inside a closed spacecraft.

Benefits and intended impact. The panel makes a complex scientific topic easy to understand for students and visitors, combining something they can see and touch with an interactive screen.

Tools used. Cardboard, paint and wooden decorations for the panel, a tablet, an application created with an AI tool, and Canva for the presentation.

Creativity. We mixed a handmade poster with digital technology, turning a simple cardboard board into an interactive “spacecraft control panel.”

Factors we considered. How to explain the science of fire clearly, how to compare Earth and space side by side, and how to make the project interactive so people want to explore it.
